steps.prompt: A pizza with diameter $12$ inches costs twice as much as one with diameter $8$ inches. Which is the better deal?

cards.title: Circles, sectors and arcs
cards.body: Area $\pi r^2$, circumference $2\pi r$. A sector with angle $\theta$ is $\frac{\theta}{360}$ of the circle: area $\frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^2$, arc length $\frac{\theta}{360} \cdot 2\pi r$. Leave answers in terms of $\pi$.

cards.title: Worked example: a sector
cards.problem: A sector has radius $6$ and angle $60^\circ$. What is its area?

try.prompt: What fraction of the circle is it?
What is the area of the sector? Write it with π.

cards.title: Shaded regions
cards.body: Build the shaded region from pieces you know: add them or take them away. A ring is $\pi R^2 - \pi r^2$. A segment (between a chord and its arc) is a sector minus a triangle. A circle that just fits in a square has diameter equal to the side.

cards.title: Worked example: circle in a square
cards.problem: A circle just fits inside a square of side $10$. What area of the square is outside the circle?

steps.text: The diameter is the side, so the radius is $5$.

try.prompt: What is the shaded area? Write it with π, like 36-9π.

cards.title: The common trap: diameter for radius
cards.body: Halve the diameter before squaring. Area uses $\pi r^2$ and length uses $2\pi r$; don't mix them. And check what fraction of the circle a sector is before multiplying.
